// diagnostic

E1017

`#Inline(Always) fn` reads `context.trace`, which names the reading function's own frame

What

`#Inline(Always) fn` reads `context.trace`, which names the reading function's own frame

Why

`#Inline(Always)` guarantees every direct call is inlined on every tier, and `context.trace` starts at the frame of the function that reads it, while an inlined copy runs in its caller's frame. Sema refuses each mark that can't keep the guarantee: a call of itself or a cycle of marked calls (E0917), a use as a value (E0918), a body over the size ceiling (E0919), `#Scrub` (E1016), a read of `context.trace` (E1017) and a foreign body (E1021)

Fix

Drop `#Inline(Always)`, or read `context.trace` in the function's caller.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1017: tests/ui/inline_always_reads_trace.stderr.

Error [jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace]: `depth` reads `context.trace`, so `#Inline(Always)` cannot expand it
  --> tests/ui/inline_always_reads_trace.jet:3:46
    |
  3 | #Inline(Always) depth: fn() -> Int { context.trace.len() }
    |                                              ^^^^^
 Why: `context.trace` starts at the reading function's own frame, and an inlined copy has no frame of its own: the trace would name the caller instead. `#Inline(Always)` guarantees that every direct call is inlined on every tier, or the program is refused: sema refuses a function that calls itself or closes a cycle of marked calls (E0917), one used as a value (E0918), one over the size ceiling (E0919), a `#Scrub` routine (E1016), one that reads `context.trace` (E1017) and one with a foreign body (E1021).
 Fix: Drop `#Inline(Always)`, or read `context.trace` in the function that calls `depth`.
